claims.statement: The literal weighted Hall graph has an integer flow saturating all positive upper-layer supply on each of the first five stored eligible rank-7 census rows at each of orders 16, 17, and 18.
claims.scope: Exactly the deterministic first five eligible p=7 rows in stored order at each of orders 16, 17, and 18 in the supplied census results; 15 literal-set networks total. The selector is the fixed original strict favorable-leaf selector, the layers are independent sets of sizes 8 and 7, and legal arcs are all one-vertex deletions and the specified absent-vertex switches with exactly two neighbors in the upper set. This is finite flow feasibility only.
claims.reason: retained: an independent foreground replay from scratch copies exactly matches the stored evidence on all 15 rows. It reconstructs the trees; checks alpha, first descent, eligibility, every strict selector value, original supports, each selected term and complete S; verifies S=supply-capacity; and checks legal arcs, integral flow, node capacities, conservation totals and zero residual-cut deficit. The result is retained only for this finite deterministic prefix.

limitations: Only the first five eligible stored rows at each of orders 16, 17 and 18 were flow-tested; no claim is made about the remaining 4,976 eligible p=7 rows.
Census generation was not rerun; the finite result depends on the two supplied hash-pinned census result files.
The finite flows establish neither a universal weighted Hall mechanism nor the primary aggregate for all eligible ordinary trees; no formal or authoritative status is proposed.
